# Course metrics: the only source for presentation numbers

<!-- Generated by scripts/course_metrics.py from evaluations/study_registry.json and each run's metrics.json. Do not edit by hand: run `uv run python scripts/course_metrics.py`. -->

Every number in the course documents (decks, demo scripts, report, marker guide) is quoted from this file. Only runs the registry marks **current** are listed; superseded and exploratory runs are named at the end and are not presentation evidence. Values are shown to at most four decimal places; exact values are in `metrics.json` next to this file. No study measures a real business outcome yet: every number below is a historical backtest, a simulation, a published benchmark, or an offline evaluation, as its data kind says.

Registry reviewed on 2026-10-27.

## E1 — `E1-20261026T200641Z`

Data kind: simulation (real UCI scope; terms, stock and CO2 factors assumed or simulated). Source: `artifacts/experiments/E1-20261026T200641Z/metrics.json`.

Headline (registry review): Under a binding budget, a 5% CO2 cut is almost free (9 of 23,980 units), but halving CO2 costs 13.8 points of coverage

Notes (registry review): Real UCI scope (40 SKUs, two offers each, £20,000 weekly budget); CO2 lane factors and unit weights are assumed, terms and stock simulated. Exact epsilon-constraint (CP-SAT, 21 caps, 3.1 s) against NSGA-II (pymoo, 3 seeds): NSGA-II reaches 98.1-98.5% of the exact front's hypervolume but 35-43 of its ~116 front points are dominated by exact points. The exact front is sampled at 21 caps, so its hypervolume is a lower bound.

## FA1 — `FA1-20261026T200912Z`

Data kind: simulation (real UCI scope and country shares; stock, terms and budget simulated). Source: `artifacts/experiments/FA1-20261026T200912Z/metrics.json`.

Headline (registry review): Under a binding budget, rest-of-world customers got 51% coverage against 83% for UK customers; moderate reweighing (alpha 0.4) cuts the gap from 31.7 to 12.2 points for 1.4 points of total coverage

Notes (registry review): Real UCI scope and recorded country shares (365 days); stock, terms and budget simulated; demand is the champion forecast. A product's shortfall is attributed to its customers by past purchase share. Worst-to-best ratio 0.62 before, 0.85 at alpha 0.4 (passes the four-fifths screen). Full inverse-share reweighing (alpha 1) over-corrects: UK falls to 72% and total coverage drops 7 points. One scope, one date; deterministic allocation.

## JS1 — `JS1-20261030T191602Z`

Data kind: simulation (assumed routes and handling times; published ft06 check). Source: `artifacts/experiments/JS1-20261030T191602Z/metrics.json`.

Headline (registry review): Each hand dispatch rule (FIFO, SPT, EDD, most work remaining) gives a receiving-floor schedule 11-13 % longer on average than exact CP-SAT; even the best rule chosen after the fact is 8.5 % longer (1.6-13.8 %), and no single rule is best at every size

Notes (registry review): Check: the Fisher-Thompson ft06 instance solves to its known optimum of 55 in 0.01 s (rules 61-88). Nine receiving-floor instances (10, 20, 40 orders x 3) on four stations; routes, handling minutes and due slots ASSUMED, order volumes from real UCI weekly sales. CP-SAT (8 workers, 20 s) proved 7 of 9 makespans optimal. Minimising total tardiness instead, the rules' tardiness is 32 % (SPT) to 436 % (MWKR) higher. Static one-shift job shop; no breakdowns or late arrivals.

## PM1 — `PM1-20261030T192104Z`

Data kind: published benchmark (AI4I 2020, a synthetic dataset) and simulation (motor fleet). Source: `artifacts/experiments/PM1-20261030T192104Z/metrics.json`.

Headline (registry review): On the AI4I 2020 dataset LightGBM catches 61 of 71 test failures with 135 inspections (AUC 0.98), cutting expected cost 72 % against running to failure; on a simulated motor fleet, replacing on predicted life avoids every failure at two-thirds the cost of fixed intervals, though a 1D-CNN does not beat a ridge baseline

Notes (registry review): (a) UCI AI4I 2020 (CC BY 4.0, synthetic data modelled on a milling process), 10,000 cycles, 339 failures; 60/20/20 random split; threshold chosen on validation by assumed costs (missed failure GBP 2,000, inspection GBP 150). Logistic regression AUC 0.93, average precision 0.43; LightGBM AUC 0.98, average precision 0.86. Heat, power and overstrain failures all caught; tool-wear failures 1 of 10 and random failures 0 of 4, as their causes are random by construction. (b) Simulated fleet, 80 training and 30 test motors; RMSE ridge 18.9, CNN 19.3 cycles: a negative result for deep learning on this signal. Policies on the 30 test motors: run to failure GBP 72,000 (30 failures); fixed interval at the 5th life percentile GBP 18,000 (3 failures, 94 cycles of life discarded on average); replace when predicted life < 20 cycles GBP 12,000 (0 failures, 16 cycles discarded). Costs assumed.

## QC1 — `QC1-20261030T193358Z`

Data kind: simulation (generated images). Source: `artifacts/experiments/QC1-20261030T193358Z/metrics.json`.

Headline (registry review): On generated goods-in images a small CNN flags defects with AUC 0.997 against 0.946 for hand-made features; letting it pass items and checking only what it flags costs 53 % less than inspecting everything, with 98.7 % of defects caught

Notes (registry review): Images generated from stated rules (glaze texture, printed band, uneven light, noise; 30 % carry a scratch, chip or stain, some faint): 6,000 train, 1,500 validation, 3,000 test. Threshold chosen on validation by assumed costs (manual check GBP 0.30, escaped defect GBP 12). CNN: 958 flagged, 11 escapes, precision 0.89; inspect-all GBP 900 vs CNN policy GBP 419. The hand-made-feature baseline reaches the same recall only by flagging 95 % of items. Occlusion maps (drop in the CNN's logit when each 8x8 patch is greyed out) show the score depends on the defect region. Generated images are easier than real photographs: a method check.

## W1 — `W1-20261027T055557Z`

Data kind: historical backtest (UCI sales; Open-Meteo weather). Source: `artifacts/experiments/W1-20261027T055557Z/metrics.json`.

Headline (registry review): On total daily units, XGBoost beats Prophet and a seasonal naive (WAPE 24.6% vs 28.0% and 29.7%); adding London weather makes no clear difference to either (95% intervals span zero)

Notes (registry review): 13 weekly origins from 2011-09-05 to 2011-11-28, 7 days ahead, 91 total-level points and 4,550 product-day points (50 products). Product-level daily demand is intermittent, so WAPE is above 100% for every model (XGBoost 110%, naive 114%) and MAPE is taken over non-zero days only. Weather on the target day is the observed value, so any gain would be an upper bound. Daily correlation of units with mean temperature -0.03 and with rainfall 0.05. Weather: Open-Meteo historical API, CC BY 4.0.
